records.quote: Suppose X and Z are two random variables with cdf's G and F respectively. Survival functions G_bar = 1-G and F_bar = 1-F and densities g and f. Then X is said to be smaller than Z in stochastic order (X <=st Z) if G_bar(x) <= F_bar(x) for all x >= 0; in likelihood ratio order (X <=lr Z) if g(x)/f(x) is decreasing in all x >= 0; hazard rate order (X <=hr Z) if G_bar(x)/F_bar(x) is decreasing in all x >= 0; reversed hazard rate order (X <=rh Z) if G(x)/F(x) is decreasing in all x >= 0. These four stochastic orders are related as X <=rh Z <= X <=lr Z => X <=hr Z => X <=st Z.
records.family: Lehmann Type II Frechet Poisson distribution LFP(alpha, nu, gamma, omega)

conclusion.direction: X <=_rh Z <= X <=_lr Z => X <=_hr Z => X <=_st Z (lr implies hr and rh; hr implies st)
